question: Which of the following may be measured through a Reaumur Scale?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Temperature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Réaumur scale, commonly known as the **"octogesimal division,**" is a temperature scale that defines the melting and boiling temperatures of water as 0 and 80 degrees Celsius, respectively.
 
• **René Antoine Ferchault de Réaumur, **who developed a comparable scale in 1730, is honoured by the scale's name.
 
• Its principal current applications include **monitoring milk temperature during cheese manufacturing** in Italian and Swiss companies, and measuring temperature when heating sugar syrup for pastries and sweets in the Netherlands.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• René-Antoine Ferchault de Réaumur, a French scientist, invented the Réaumur temperature scale in** 1730**.
 
• **With its zero **set at the freezing point of water and **its 80° mark at the boiling point of water** at normal atmospheric pressure.
